correctness.rationale: With r=2s even, theta G_r is bipartite so Q is conjugate to L. The difference of the two short-path midvertices is a Laplacian eigenline of eigenvalue 2. Decomposing its complement under terminal reflection gives an s-dimensional antisymmetric and (s+2)-dimensional symmetric irreducible Jacobi matrix. Their continuants are F_-=p_s+p_{s-1} and F_+=(t^2+2t-8)p_s+(2t-t^2)p_{s-1}, where t=2-lambda and p_{j+1}=t p_j-p_{j-1}. Shared roots would require t=+/-2 but those cannot annihilate F_-, hence only lambda=2 can be repeated; F_+(0)=0 iff s odd. Direct distances show metric dimension 3 for r=2,4 and 2 for even r>=6. Independent exact graph Laplacian factorization and exhaustive resolving-set BFS checked r=2,4,6,8,10, giving multiplicity pattern (2,1,2,1,2) and metric dimensions (3,3,2,2,2).

originality.rationale: The metric dimension is already classified in 2022 work and not claimed new. Alfuraidan et al. 2026 treats r odd in Theta_{2,2,r} and poses broader equality problem. Paone–Paone 2026 Cor 8.1 covers multiplicity of signless-Laplacian eigenvalue 2 on generalized theta graphs, but this does not by itself prove all other eigenvalues simple and determine maximal multiplicities/equality for even r. The precise even-branch all-spectrum rigidity is best-of-knowledge uncovered, with an inaccessible same-graph paper explicit risk.
